source.title: Learning and generalization of one-hidden-layer neural networks, going beyond standard Gaussian data
source.authors: Hong-Kang Li; Shuai Zhang; M. Wang

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports gradient-descent convergence for a one-hidden-layer teacher-student network under Gaussian-mixture inputs, bearing on V1's training-convergence claim through a different setting and analysis. It does not test the benchmark or corrupted-label conditions in V1.
record.gate_note: The study's theoretical convergence and simulation results for its proposed tensor initialization plus gradient descent bear on V1. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows. The sample-complexity plots test sample requirements for recovery and do not separately measure training classification error.
record.test_reason: The study proves and illustrates weight recovery and convergence for a shallow sigmoid teacher-student network with tensor initialization. These outcomes do not measure V1's training classification error, V2's width-dependent spurious minima, or any other version. References to residual networks and batch normalization are background.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors establish linear convergence for their tensor-initialized gradient-descent algorithm, approximate teacher-weight recovery, generalization guarantees, and sample complexity dependent on Gaussian-mixture parameters.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a one-hidden-layer sigmoid teacher-student network, Gaussian-mixture inputs, cross-entropy, and tensor initialization before gradient descent. It does not use benchmark CNNs or random initialization.
record.method_sensitivity: Input distribution parameters affect sample complexity and convergence rate; increasing the mixture mean magnitude increases sample complexity and slows convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: With sufficient samples, tensor initialization followed by gradient descent converges linearly to a critical point near a permutation of the teacher weights.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shallow sigmoid teacher networks with Gaussian-mixture inputs admit provable approximate weight recovery using tensor initialization and gradient descent.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing Gaussian-mixture mean magnitudes slows convergence in the theorem and the simulation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-distribution parameters affect gradient-descent convergence speed in shallow sigmoid teacher-student networks.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Conference on Information Sciences and Systems
record.problems: The empirical convergence illustration is figure-only and gives no numeric values in the text. The reported outcomes concern convergence and weight recovery rather than training classification error; the algorithm uses tensor initialization rather than random initialization.
record.rows_left_out: The sample-complexity experiments in Section V.A, Figures 1–2 report success rates for estimation across dimensions and mixture means, not training classification error or a direct convergence outcome; no rows recorded.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in randomly initialized CNNs, including corrupted labels and the stated model-size and training-recipe conditions.
Spurious-minimum frequencies in ReLU teacher-student networks and their reduction with extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation and its prevention through identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonality, and trainable depth.
Training above the initial stability limit, curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability behavior, and divergence.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V1 limits_scope labels should be removed. Measuring a different outcome does not demonstrate a limitation of V1. Figures 1–2 are already declared in rows_left_out and supply no additional test of the listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, convolutional networks, random or corrupted labels, SGD or Adam, or the effects of smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes.

rows.subject: Algorithm 1 with tensor initialization
rows.size_stated: one hidden layer with K neurons; simulation uses 3 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent minimizes empirical cross-entropy risk after tensor initialization.

conditions.value: convergence to a critical point near a permutation of teacher weights

rows.measure: Iterates' convergence and distance to teacher weights
rows.value: Linear convergence to a critical point; distance bounded by O(K^(5/2)·√(d log n/n)).
rows.note: The theorem concerns recovery of teacher weights and convergence, not training classification error reaching zero. The model is initialized by a tensor method, not random initialization.
rows.check: Weight recovery and linear convergence to a critical point cannot establish near-zero training classification error. The model is fully connected with sigmoid activations and tensor initialization. Section II explicitly allows the teacher weights to differ from the empirical-risk optimum. This is a result about the proposed algorithm, not evidence for a listed version.

rows.subject: Algorithm 1 with tensor initialization
rows.size_stated: one hidden layer with 3 neurons; d = 5
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent convergence experiment with varying Gaussian-mixture mean magnitude.
rows.value: Figure 3 is described as showing linear convergence for different µ̃; convergence slows as µ̃ increases.
rows.note: Figure values are not transcribed. The text reports linear convergence and slower convergence with increasing µ̃; it does not report training classification error.
rows.check: Distance to the converged weights measures convergence speed, not training classification error. Varying input means does not test activation-matched initialization or batch normalization. Three hidden neurons are specified in Section V.A but not explicitly restated for Section V.B.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
